name: ClickHouse
summary: A column-oriented analytical database that organizes data into sorted parts, executes expressions in vectors, and merges immutable parts in the background.

features.name: Column-oriented storage
features.description: ClickHouse stores table data by columns and its MergeTree family organizes inserted data into sorted parts, making columns and parts explicit units of analytical storage.
benefits: Efficiently reads only columns needed by analytical queries
Makes sorted data parts suitable for large scans
costs: Write and schema choices are optimized for analytical access patterns

features.name: Vectorized expression execution
features.description: The ClickHouse query pipeline processes data in blocks and evaluates expressions over columns of values, exposing a vectorized unit between storage and query operators.
benefits: Supports high-throughput analytical scans and transformations
costs: Batch-oriented execution is less directly suited to point-oriented workloads
Operators must manage block sizing and materialization

features.name: Background data-part merging
features.description: MergeTree tables continually merge data parts in the background; the merge process combines sorted parts into larger parts and applies configured data transformations such as deduplication or aggregation where supported.
benefits: Converts many small writes into fewer read-efficient parts
Moves compaction work out of foreground query execution
costs: Background I/O and CPU compete with queries and inserts
Read visibility and storage shape depend on merge progress

mathematical_views.question: How can a relational query be represented as transformations over selected columns and finite blocks?
assumptions: Each operator preserves the intended relational semantics
Blocks are finite partitions of a logical stream
Physical compression and hardware effects are abstracted

mathematical_views.question: Under what conditions can a set of sorted data parts be replaced by a larger part while preserving the table's query-visible semantics?
assumptions: Parts have compatible table metadata and ordering
Merge transformations implement the table-engine contract
The view abstracts replication and failure recovery

costs: Analytical layout and part management constrain write patterns
Batch execution adds workload-specific buffering and tuning
